transcript.text: Alright, let's get the capacity review started. Before I can approve the current draft policy for the image-processing pipeline, I need to hear from each area. FinOps, SRE, security, and customer support — what operational requirements do we need to account for? The draft has 12 baseline workers, scales out at 100 queued jobs, uses any available region, and runs a single FIFO queue for all customers. I need to know if any of you see issues with that before we go to production ahead of the seasonal traffic increase.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While reconciling this month's cloud invoice for another service, I confirmed that the available compute reservation applies to this pipeline only with exactly 18 baseline workers and a monthly capacity ceiling of exactly 24000 USD. The draft's 12-worker plan has no reservation commitment, and I have not yet updated the capacity proposal to reflect this.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag something from a load investigation I ran this morning. During testing of the expected burst pattern, I measured an 11-minute worker startup time. To keep processing latency within our operating target, the pipeline needs exactly 6 warm workers with scale-out triggered at exactly 40 queued jobs. I have not yet filed this result in the capacity review. The current draft's 12 baseline workers and 100-job scale-out threshold don't account for this — the scale-out trigger is too high and will allow latency to exceed target before new workers come online, especially given that 11-minute startup delay.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a security constraint I found while checking the image-processing deployment manifest for an unrelated access review. Customer-uploaded image data must run in exactly eu-central-1 and use the tenant-managed KMS key named tenant_kms. The current draft permits any available processing region and does not specify the required KMS key, so it does not meet these requirements. I have not yet opened the security finding in the capacity review.

commitments.detail: Update the capacity proposal to reflect 18 baseline workers and the 24000 USD monthly capacity ceiling to secure the compute reservation.
File the load investigation results in the capacity review and update the policy to include 6 warm workers and a scale-out trigger at 40 queued jobs.
Open the security finding in the capacity review and update the policy to restrict processing to eu-central-1 with the tenant_kms KMS key.
Add the Lumen Media dedicated priority queue requirement to the capacity proposal and update the policy to enable a priority queue for Lumen Media.
